newsitem.title: UK: B.A.T retreats amid fresh U.S. legal moves.
newsitem.headline: B.A.T retreats amid fresh U.S. legal moves.

text.p: Shares in B.A.T Industries Plc fell on Thursday, bucking a firm trend in the market overall after the latest twists in the long-running saga of lawsuits against tobacco companies in the United States.
The stock was down 11p at 522-1/2 by 1345 GMT, backtracking from its 44-1/2p rise through the past four sessions. By contrast the FTSE 100 index was up 23.4 points at 4,324.9.

In a ruling that could set an important precedent for anti-tobacco cases, a Mississippi judge ruled that internal documents from Brooke Group Ltd's Liggett Group could be turned over to plaintiffs in a $650 million second-hand smoke lawsuit.
Separately in Florida a judge ordered Liggett to deliver internal industry documents for possible use in that state's lawsuit against U.S. tobacco companies.
Florida attorney general Bob Butterworth said the 20 documents would be made public if the judge agreed that public health issues were at stake and said they were "devastating" to the industry.

Shares in B.A.T rallied in recent sessions on the back of gains in U.S. tobacco stocks, though the company said there was no truth in reports that the industry planned a multi-million pound fighting fund to settle legal claims. There was also renewed talk that the company may be planned a demerger of its tobacco and insurance arms.
